\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{به} \fa{تدریج} (be tadrij)}{به تدریج (be tadrij)}]{\fa{به} \fa{تدریج} (be tadrij) — gradually, little by little}

\label{lesson:FA-C306-be-tadrij}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for the time, then the Persian for round the clock.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{به} \fa{تدریج}}
\textbf{\fa{به} \fa{تدریج}} (\emph{be tadrij}) — \textquotedblleft{}gradually, little by little\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{هوا} \fa{به} \fa{تدریج} \fa{سرد} \fa{شد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Havâ be tadrij sard shod.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The weather gradually turned cold.
\end{quote}

Formal; in speech \emph{kam-kam}. The adjective is \emph{tadriji} \textquotedblleft{}gradual\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{tadrij} is usually traced to Arabic \emph{tadrīj}, \textquotedblleft{}a gradual progression\textquotedblright{}; EtymDB lists no entry. \emph{be} \textquotedblleft{}to, by\textquotedblright{} is inherited Persian.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{be tadrij}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{be tadrij}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{be tadrij}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for the time, then the Persian for round the clock, then say \emph{be tadrij} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{در} \fa{همین} \fa{حال} (dar hamin hâl)}{در همین حال (dar hamin hâl)}]{\fa{در} \fa{همین} \fa{حال} (dar hamin hâl) — meanwhile, at the same time}

\label{lesson:FA-C306-dar-hamin-hal}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for round the clock, then the Persian for gradually.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{در} \fa{همین} \fa{حال}}
\textbf{\fa{در} \fa{همین} \fa{حال}} (\emph{dar hamin hâl}) — \textquotedblleft{}meanwhile, at the same time\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{من} \fa{ظرف} \fa{میشستم} \fa{و} \fa{در} \fa{همین} \fa{حال} \fa{برادرم} \fa{تلویزیون} \fa{تماشا} \fa{میکرد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Man zarf mishostam va dar hamin hâl barâdaram televiziyon tamâshâ mikard.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
I was washing the dishes, and meanwhile my brother was watching television.
\end{quote}

It joins two background actions, often both in the past continuous. Literally \textquotedblleft{}in this very state\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{hâl} \textquotedblleft{}state\textquotedblright{} is borrowed from Arabic \emph{ḥāl} (EtymDB); \emph{dar} \textquotedblleft{}in\textquotedblright{} and \emph{hamin} \textquotedblleft{}this very\textquotedblright{} are inherited Persian.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dar hamin hâl}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dar hamin hâl}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{dar hamin hâl}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for round the clock, then the Persian for gradually, then say \emph{dar hamin hâl} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \fa{در} \fa{همین} \fa{حال} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Meanwhile, at the same time\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{تا} \fa{اینکه} (tâ inke)}{تا اینکه (tâ inke)}]{\fa{تا} \fa{اینکه} (tâ inke) — until finally, until}

\label{lesson:FA-C306-ta-inke}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for gradually, then the Persian for meanwhile.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{تا} \fa{اینکه}}
\textbf{\fa{تا} \fa{اینکه}} (\emph{tâ inke}) — \textquotedblleft{}until finally, until\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{منتظر} \fa{ماندیم} \fa{تا} \fa{اینکه} \fa{اتوبوس} \fa{آمد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Montazer mândim tâ inke otobus âmad.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
We waited until the bus finally came.
\end{quote}

In a story it marks the turn: \emph{... tâ inke yek ruz ...} \textquotedblleft{}... until one day ...\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{tâ} \textquotedblleft{}until\textquotedblright{} is inherited: EtymDB traces it through Middle Persian to Old Persian \emph{yātā}, \textquotedblleft{}until, so that\textquotedblright{}. \emph{inke} is \emph{in} \textquotedblleft{}this\textquotedblright{} + \emph{ke} \textquotedblleft{}that\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tâ inke}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tâ inke}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{tâ inke}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for gradually, then the Persian for meanwhile, then say \emph{tâ inke} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{طی} (tey)}{طی (tey)}]{\fa{طی} (tey) — during, in the space of}

\label{lesson:FA-C306-tey}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for meanwhile, then the Persian for until finally.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{طی}}
\textbf{\fa{طی}} (\emph{tey}) — \textquotedblleft{}during, in the space of\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{طی} \fa{سفر} \fa{چند} \fa{بار} \fa{باران} \fa{آمد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Tey-e safar chand bâr bârân âmad.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
It rained several times during the trip.
\end{quote}

Formal, with the ezafe: \emph{tey-e do sâl} \textquotedblleft{}over two years\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{tey} is borrowed from Arabic \emph{ṭayy} (EtymDB lists the Arabic word), usually glossed \textquotedblleft{}a folding up, a covering of distance\textquotedblright{}: time folded up as it passes.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{مجددا} (mojaddadan)}{مجددا (mojaddadan)}]{\fa{مجددا} (mojaddadan) — again, anew (formal)}

\label{lesson:FA-C306-mojaddadan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for until finally, then the Persian for during.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{مجددا}}
\textbf{\fa{مجددا}} (\emph{mojaddadan}) — \textquotedblleft{}again, anew (formal)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{او} \fa{مجددا} \fa{به} \fa{آن} \fa{شرکت} \fa{زنگ} \fa{زد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{U mojaddadan be ân sherkat zang zad.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
She phoned that company again.
\end{quote}

Formal and official; in speech \emph{dobâre}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{mojaddadan} is the Arabic adverb of \emph{mujaddad}, \textquotedblleft{}renewed\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB lists Arabic \emph{mujaddad}), made with the ending \emph{-an}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
